name: io.github.zorcec/vibeflow
title: Vibeflow
description: Task management for AI coding agents over MCP — board, CLI tools, plus UI annotation.

packageArguments.name: mcp
packageArguments.description: Run the MCP server over stdio.

packageArguments.name: --project
packageArguments.description: Project root this server serves. Required, and resolved once at startup: one process serves exactly one repository, so every tool call reads and writes that project's task store. Point it at your own repo.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.longDescription: Task management for AI coding agents over MCP and CLI. Agents claim sequenced tasks, implement, and submit for review; humans get a local-first kanban board. UI annotation files tickets with selector, file and line; verification gates the review.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.transport: stdio, one process per project. An HTTP transport also exists (vibeflow serve, MCP at /api/mcp) but it is a local loopback server, not a public endpoint, so this manifest declares no remotes.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: None. Local-first: no login is required and no API key is needed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.releaseNote: This manifest is pinned to 0.20.0, the published version of @vibeflow-tools/cli. Verified against the installed package, not the repository: an MCP `tools/list` handshake against `@vibeflow-tools/cli@0.20.0` returns 12 tools, and those names match `packages/cli/src/mcp/manifest.ts` exactly. The `tools` count here therefore matches the README's tool table.
